chapter: Army band, Lena Horne, Billie Holiday and the 1950s
title: House band at the Million Dollar Theatre in Los Angeles
summary: His seven-piece house band included Teddy Buckner and Curt Bradford and backed visiting acts like Charlie Ventura's group for about a year.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: leaping back into the late forties here, you played in the Million Dollar Theatre in Los Angeles?
Right. I was the house band there.
Was that a big band, or a small group?

It was a seven piece band, but it had a guy in there that I'm sure you know. You're talking about names, and he's still playin' trumpet. He looks like Louis -- Teddy Buckner. He's still in L.A. with his own group, and I had a little saxophone player. His original name was Curt Kirk Bradford, but he goes by the name now of Mustafa Hashim. But he was the first alto player after Jimmie Lunce Ford. Willie Smith with the great (unintelligible). Yeah. Curt Bradford. Excellent saxophonist. He was in the pit band, and we used to play for the different acts that came in, and one of the acts that came on stage during that time -- when we had two bands -- was Charlie Ventura.
And he had Benny Green playin' trombone with him.
And Roy Kral and Jackie Cain (Inaudible).
group. Some of those -- That was the house band at the Million Dollar Theater.
(Inaudible) for a year. It was a beautiful thing.
